meetings.title: Design crit: Insights dashboard v3
segments: Hi all, can you see my screen?
I'm sharing the Figma prototype.
Yep, we see it.
Hi, I'm here, just finishing a message. Go ahead.
Okay, thanks for coming. This is dashboard v3.
The big proposal is making Themes the default home instead of the feed. I want honest reactions.
Each theme card shows the label, a count, a trend arrow, and five representative quotes.
The idea is you can understand the theme without clicking in.
What's the order of the cards? By size?
By a mix of size and growth.
A big theme that isn't changing ranks below a smaller theme that doubled this week.
The idea is to surface what's new, not what's always been there.
And pinned themes shouldn't count toward the ranking, or they'll push everything else down the page.
Good point. Pinned themes get their own row at the top.
I like that. The big stable themes are usually things the team already knows about.
Could people pin a theme they care about, so it stays at the top regardless?
Good idea. Pinning is easy.
I'll add it to the prototype.
Marcus, sorry, you're breaking up a bit.
You sound like a robot.
Is this better? I'll switch to my phone's mic.
Okay, how about now?
Much better.
Great. New headset arrives tomorrow, I promise.
So, reactions to the cards?
I like the direction a lot.
My worry is five quotes.
It's a wall of text on every card.
I'd guess people read one or two and skip the rest.
Agreed. And the quotes are the most human part.
I'd rather see one great quote than five okay ones.
How do we pick the one great quote, though?
Right now the model picks the three to five most typical comments in the theme.
Typical isn't the same as quotable.
Could it pick the clearest one?
Short, specific, no customer names.
Priya could probably score that.
I'll ask her. For the prototype I'll pick them by hand.
Would fewer quotes also make the page faster?
Every card loads its quotes separately right now.
Yes, probably noticeably. Five quotes across twenty cards is a hundred requests on page load.
Three would help, and we could load the quotes in one batch instead of per card.
One batch, please. I'll make a note for Sam.
Fair. I can run a quick hallway test before the alignment meeting, three quotes versus five, with a handful of people from CS.
Who would you test with?
CS folks know the product too well.
Fair. Two people from CS, plus two from finance and ops who've never used the product.
The question is simple: look at a card for five seconds, then tell me what the theme is about.
Five seconds is harsh. I like it.
That's roughly how long people look at a dashboard card in real life, based on the session recordings.
The trend arrow. It's red when a theme is growing.
But not every growing theme is bad.
If people are praising the new export feature more and more, that's growth, and it's good news.
Red makes it look like an alarm.
How often do themes grow because of praise, in the pilot data?
More than I expected. When Lakeshore Bank shipped their new mobile app, the top growing theme for a week was people saying they loved the redesign.
With a red arrow, it looked like a crisis.
That's exactly the moment we'd want to celebrate, not alarm.
Could the team even share those in Slack?
Praise themes are great for morale.
Put that on the list for the share to Slack idea.
Not for v3, but later.
Oh, that's a really good point.
We baked in the assumption that feedback is complaints.
What if the arrow is neutral, just direction and size, and we add a small sentiment indicator next to the label?
Then growth and sentiment are separate signals.
How would sentiment be calculated? Per comment, then averaged?
That's my assumption, but Priya would know better.
The display would be simple, a small dot that's green, grey, or orange, with the split on hover.
Mostly positive, mixed, mostly negative.
Orange rather than red is good.
Red feels like an alarm, orange feels like 'look at this'.
I like that we're thinking about how it feels, not just what it shows.
I like that. It's more honest.
On merge and split. It's drag and drop right now.
How does anyone discover that?
I didn't notice it until you told me.
I didn't know either, honestly.
Okay, so that's two out of three people who didn't find it. That's a clear signal.
What did people do in the usability sessions when they wanted to fix a theme?
Mostly they looked for a menu on the theme card.
Three dots, or a right-click.
Nobody tried dragging. Which, now that I say it out loud, is a pretty clear answer.
So the buttons should probably live in that menu, too.
Yes. Menu on the card, buttons in the detail view, and drag and drop for people who discover it.
Yeah, discoverability is weak. I'll add explicit merge and split buttons in the theme detail, and keep drag and drop as the power user shortcut.
What happens technically when someone merges two themes?
Does the model learn from it immediately?
In the prototype it's instant, visually.
But I don't know what happens behind the scenes.
That's something to figure out with Priya.
My guess is the merge is saved immediately, and the model learns from it in the next nightly run.
As long as the user sees their change stick, they won't care when the learning happens.
Right. The important thing is the next morning's themes shouldn't undo their merge.
Oh, that would be infuriating.
Let's make sure that never happens.
Big picture question. Are we all comfortable taking Themes as default into the alignment meeting as the proposal?
I'd like design to present it there.
Can I ask what happens to existing customers?
Some of them have built their whole workflow around the feed.
Good question, and I don't have the answer yet.
That's something to raise at the alignment meeting.
Tom will have a view on it.
I'll add a slide on it, so we don't forget.
One question for the alignment meeting.
Do we present Themes-first as decided, or as a proposal?
As a proposal with a strong recommendation.
Tom and Aisha haven't seen it yet, and they'll have good questions about existing customers.
I'd rather they feel part of the decision than have it handed to them.
That's a good call. People support what they help shape.
Yes. I think it's the right call.
Yes. It's the story we want to tell, too.
Great. I'll update the prototype with neutral arrows, sentiment, and the buttons, and present it at the alignment meeting.
What about mobile? Do we need a mobile version of the themes home for the beta?
I don't think so. Almost all usage is desktop, and the beta audience is product and CX teams at their desks.
I'd make it readable on a phone, but not optimized.
Agreed. Readable, not optimized.
Okay, thanks everyone, this was really useful.
I'll send the updated prototype before the alignment meeting.
